Yesterday the day-ahead price ran from its floor at 12:00 to its ceiling at 18:00.

🌞 Solar 8.8% (licensed 1.8% + unlicensed 7.0%)
💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 32.4%
🍃 Wind 5.6%
🔥 Natural gas only 16.3%
🌱 Total renewables 52.4% — all fossil 47.6%

🌙 18:00 → 4,500 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 42,426 MWh

Between 11:00, when solar output was highest, and 18:00, demand rose 2,265 MWh and solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 12,133 MWh. Hydro, wind and other renewables added 7,493 MWh and fossil plants added 6,589 MWh.

The largest hourly cost came at 13:00, with 1,149.6 MWh of up-regulation: on the published supply curve, buying that volume in the day-ahead market would have lifted the clearing price to 3,449 TL/MWh.

📆 Versus 30 October 2026, a Friday against a Saturday: the daily average was 3,487 TL/MWh and the floor 2,501 TL/MWh, at 02:00–03:00 rather than 12:00.
📆 Versus 24 October 2026, the same weekday one week earlier: the daily average was 3,666 TL/MWh and the floor 1,850 TL/MWh, also at 12:00.

Wind stayed under 30 October's low of 5,525 MW and 24 October's reported low of 12,155 MW.

🍃 Wind 5,293 MW at 00:00, falling to 1,953 MW at 14:30
🔥 Natural gas 9,992 MW at 03:00, rising to 16,016 MW at 17:00
☀️ Solar peaked at 6,489 MW at 12:00 and was at zero from 17:00
💧 Pumped storage peaked at 497 MW at 16:30 and was at zero from 08:30 to 15:30
⚛️ Nuclear moved between 5,117 MW and 5,138 MW across the day
🏠 National demand 21,083 MW at 05:30, rising to 33,348 MW at 17:30
🔌 Interconnectors: net import of 4,738 MW at 08:00, 5,468 MW at 12:00, 2,378 MW at 15:30 and 2,388 MW at 17:30

Between 12:00 and 17:30 national demand rose by 7,608 MW while solar fell to zero. TÜRKİYE · DAY-END SCORECARD · 30 October 2026
Yesterday the balancing price sat below the day-ahead price in most hours.

🎯 Balancing vs day-ahead: the balancing price was below the day-ahead price in 18 hours, above it in 3, equal in 3.

📊 The day's generation mix (EPİAŞ):
🌞 Solar 8.2% (licensed 1.4% + unlicensed 6.7%)
💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 30.7%
🍃 Wind 10.3%
🔥 Natural gas only 16.0%
🌱 Total renewables 54.5% — all fossil 45.5%

📉 The price (MCP, Market Clearing Price):
🌙 02:00–03:00 → 2,501 TL/MWh, the floor of the day, with demand at 30,277 MWh at 02:00
🌙 17:00–19:00 → 4,500 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 43,462 MWh at 17:00
Daily average 3,487 TL/MWh.

From the solar peak at 11:00 to 17:00, the first hour of the ceiling, demand barely moved, down 437 MWh, and solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 11,147 MWh. Over the same hours hydro, wind and other renewables rose 5,935 MWh and fossil output rose 4,556 MWh.

⚡ Balancing cost 20,837,381 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. The largest hourly cost came at 06:00, 2,454,760 TL, when 1,102 MWh was instructed down and the SMP (System Marginal Price), the balancing price, cleared at 890 TL/MWh. That is surplus energy real time did not need, and day-ahead buying cannot close it.

📆 Versus 29 October 2026: daily average 3,053 TL/MWh, floor 2,020 TL/MWh at 04:00.
📆 Versus 23 October 2026, the same weekday one week earlier: daily average 3,242 TL/MWh, floor 250 TL/MWh at 12:00.

💡 What it means:
A first reading: the climb in the day-ahead price from 07:00 to 08:00 is consistent with the morning rise in demand, which grew 6,209 MWh in that hour, more than solar and hydro, wind and other renewables added together. What fossil plants had left to cover, consumption minus solar, hydro, wind and other renewables, rose 2,828 MWh over the same hour.

🔥 Natural gas 19,369 MW at 17:30, falling to 13,101 MW at 23:30

🔌 Interconnectors: net export of 2,896 MW at 07:30, import of 1,490 MW at 11:30 and 72 MW at 17:00, export of 46 MW at 18:00

From the 11:30 solar peak to the 17:00 evening national-demand peak, national demand rose 7,818 MW as solar set; GB solar is almost all embedded, so when it sets national demand rises by much of the same amount. 📆 Versus 22 October 2026 at the same half hour, the Thursday before: wind 4,899 MW against 5,282 MW, system short in both, 230.5 MWh against 14.9 MWh.

Which plant prices a long half hour changes with what is running. At 16:00 the bids setting the opening-line prices came from pumped storage on 29 October 2026 and wind farms on 28 October 2026, with wind at 4,186 MW against 11,234 MW, gas at 18,841 MW against 15,053 MW, pumped storage generating 410 MW against none and solar at 405 MW against 377 MW. National demand was flat between the two days, 33,611 MW against 34,332 MW.

TÜRKİYE · DAY-AHEAD OUTLOOK · 31 October 2026
Tomorrow's net load swing is narrower than the past month's median.

📉 Net load, once wind and solar are taken out of the load plan, is lowest at 12:00 at 23,371 MWh, while the evening reaches 39,627 MWh. The swing between them is 16,256 MWh, which is 5.2% narrower than the median swing of the 30 days from 30 September to 29 October 2026.

⚙️ LOWEST NET LOAD. 12:00 to 12:59 is the day's very low net load band. The lower of the Market Clearing Price (MCP) and the System Marginal Price (SMP) was at or below 150 TL/MWh in the 12:00 hour on 14 separate days from 30 September to 29 October 2026.

⚙️ HIGHEST NET LOAD. 17:00 to 21:59 is the day's very high net load band. The higher of MCP and SMP reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 36 hours across 15 separate days in that window over the same dates.

🔎 WHAT STANDS OUT
Net load is at 36,433 MWh or higher in every hour of the very high band. The low band lasts one hour, the high band five.

💡 What it means: the plants that fill in after wind and solar have less ground to cover than on a typical day.

METHOD
📐 Net load = load plan − wind forecast − solar
🌞 Solar: no EPİAŞ forecast exists; shaped from the mean realised profile of 23 October to 29 October 2026 (7 complete days)
📊 Bands: quintiles of the look-back window, not of the target day

Source: EPİAŞ Transparency Platform, 30 October 2026

GREAT BRITAIN · DAY-AHEAD OUTLOOK · 31 October 2026
Wind opens at its strongest and reaches its low twice, the second time deeper.

📉 The wind trajectory for 31 October 2026, as published by the system operator:
The day opens at its highest reading, 5,194 MW at 00:00, and every step from 00:00→01:00 to 04:00→05:00 is a fall. The forecast stays low through the morning and early afternoon, with its lowest readings across 12:00 to 15:00, rises to a second high across 18:00 to 21:00, and closes at 3,345 MW at 23:00. The distance from the lowest reading to the highest is 2,365 MW.

⚙️ LOWEST WIND. 12:00-14:59, between 2,829 MW and 2,898 MW. No single lowest hour is named: 12:00, 13:00 and 14:00 in the block and 15:00 after it sit within 3% of one another. At least two of the day's three lowest readings fall in this block. The third place is open among a block hour and 15:00, 11:00, 05:00 and 06:00 outside it, which sit within 3% of 12:00; 10:00 sits more than 3% above 12:00.

⚙️ HIGHEST WIND. 00:00-02:59, between 3,853 MW and 5,194 MW. The day's three highest readings all fall in this block, at 00:00, 01:00 and 02:00 in that order, each more than 3% from the next. Every reading after 02:00 sits more than 3% below it.

🔎 WHAT STANDS OUT

The day has a second low. The opening fall stops at 05:00, at 2,947 MW; every step from 05:00→06:00 to 07:00→08:00 is a rise and every step from 08:00→09:00 to 13:00→14:00 is a fall, to readings at 13:00 and 14:00 that sit more than 3% below 05:00.

Between the lows the forecast never climbs more than 148 MW above the 05:00 reading, and the eleven readings from 05:00 to 15:00 span 266 MW. The lowest three-hour block sits on the later low and leaves 05:00 outside it.

METHOD
📐 Figures are the system operator's day-ahead wind forecast, in MW, read on the hour in local time
🌬️ Wind forecast is transmission-connected output only
🔌 Distribution-connected wind and solar are not metered by the system operator; they appear as reduced national demand rather than as generation
📊 Peak demand is published as a single daily figure, not a half-hourly curve

SOURCES

The distance from the lowest reading to the highest is 2,697 MW.

⚙️ LOWEST WIND. 14:00-16:59, between 5,822 MW and 6,000 MW. The day's lowest reading is the closing one at 23:00, outside the block and more than 3% below every other hour. The next places are not ranked: 15:00, 16:00 and 14:00, all in the block, sit within 3% of one another, and 22:00, at 6,090 MW outside the block, sits within 3% of 16:00 and 14:00. Of the day's three lowest readings, the second is one of the three block hours and the third is a block hour or 22:00.

⚙️ HIGHEST WIND. 07:00-09:59, between 8,182 MW and 8,323 MW. At least two of the day's three highest readings fall in the block; the remaining one is either in it or at 06:00, the hour before it.

🔎 WHAT STANDS OUT

The day's lowest single reading falls at the close, outside its lowest three-hour block. The closing reading is 196 MW below the reading at 15:00 and 287 MW below the reading at 16:00.
